claim.why_it_matters: This page otherwise preserves indentation with '    ', but the two continuation lines at the top of each print column lose it. 'Implicit 639' continues 'SET statement' from the foot of page 1255 and 'In formats 30' is a sub-entry of 'Special character words 105'; both are promoted to top-level entries.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed by rendering spec_p1256.png at 300 dpi and measuring the left-edge x of every text line. On this page the two-column index uses exactly two indent stops: left column top-level entries begin at x=266 px and sub-entries at x=339-341 px; right column top-level entries begin at x=1272 px and sub-entries at x=1343-1346 px. The first printed line of the left column, 'Implicit  639', begins at x=341 -- the SUB-ENTRY stop, not the top-level stop. The first printed line of the right column, 'In formats  30', begins at x=1346 -- again the sub-entry stop. A cropped visual of both column heads corroborates the measurement: both first lines are visibly inset relative to 'Shared files' / 'Shared memory area' and 'Special insertion editing' / 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph' respectively. The markdown (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 52729 and 52788) writes both lines flush left with no ' ' prefix, while using '    ' for all 30+ other sub-entries on the same page -- so this is not the transcription's convention being applied differently, it is the convention being dropped on exactly these two lines. The parentage in the claim also checks out: page 1255 ends with 'SET statement [71], [505], [729]' followed by the indented ' x4 Dynamic-capacity tables [157]', so the indented 'Implicit 639' is the next alphabetical sub-entry of SET statement; 'In formats 30' immediately follows the left column's last line 'Special character words  105' and is its sub-entry. Both quotes in the claim are accurate to their sources. This is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation: in an index the indent stop IS the encoding of hierarchy, and its loss converts two sub-entries into two spurious top-level entries ('Implicit' and 'In formats' as standalone index heads), which changes what the transcription asserts. Severity is correctly cosmetic -- the back-of-book index is a non-normative navigation aid and no language semantics, syntax, or general rule is affected.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but the kind label is imprecise: nothing is misplaced or lost as text -- both lines are present and in the correct reading order, including the blank line that legitimately marks the print-column break. The defect is LOST INDENTATION (lost index hierarchy) on exactly two lines: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 52729 'Implicit [639](#page-639)' and line 52788 'In formats [30](#page-30)' should each carry the page's standard sub-entry prefix '    '. Measured evidence at 300 dpi: left column top-level x=266 vs sub-entry x=339-341, and 'Implicit' sits at x=341; right column top-level x=1272 vs sub-entry x=1343-1346, and 'In formats' sits at x=1346. Cause is the well-known one for this transcription -- the first line of each print column, being a continuation of a sub-entry list broken across a column or page boundary, loses its indent. Fix is a two-line prefix insertion; no text content changes.
